A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMPARTAIL work and share matching headline experiments. v1 ends after the references; v2 includes appendices in Sections 7–12. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and Tables 1–4 report original Action Genome experiments comparing IMPARTAIL adaptations with baselines, including corrupted-input evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional mask-setting ablations, predicate-level results, and detailed robustness results in Figure 5 and Tables 5–34.

M1.justification: The architecture and selective-loss principle remain. However, v1 Algorithm 1 samples a retained subset, whereas v2 Algorithm 2 explicitly samples labels to remove. v2 also uses opposite mask conventions in its main-text and appendix losses. These inconsistencies prevent reliably distinguishing an intentional procedural revision from documentation errors.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Action Genome using VidSGG, SGA, their existing grounding modes, and corrupted-input counterparts. v1 already reports evaluation across 16 corruption scenarios; the additional appendix scores do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained: STTran and DSGDetr for VidSGG; STTran++, DSGDetr++, and SceneSayer ODE/SDE for clean SGA; and the STTran/DSGDetr + and ++ variants for robust SGA. Appendix comparisons retain these corresponding sets. TEMPURA and FloCoDe discussion does not introduce new evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Tables 5–31 introduce systematic S=70,40,10 configurations, extend reported SGA F settings from 0.5/0.7 to include 0.3/0.9, and add evaluation at K=100. Section 5 also states that reported results use fixed 0.9 masking, whereas v1 describes progressive masking. This changes the reported experimental specification without establishing that headline experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 provides baseline comparisons and corruption tests but no mask-setting ablation. v2 adds extensive masking-sensitivity analyses across models and settings in Sections 11–12, a fixed-versus-progressive masking comparison in Section 5, and predicate-level clean-versus-corrupted recall analysis in Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The additional tables retain point estimates and relative percentage changes rather than introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and matched robustness entries retain their values, while v2 adds extensive ablation results, recall columns, K=100 scores, and predicate-level findings. For example, new Table 6 reports STTran SGCLS with-constraint R@10 of 44.9 for the baseline versus 39.9 with IMPARTAIL at S=10, alongside the previously reported mR@10 values of 25.0 and 32.3.

T1.justification: The task definitions, object-continuity assumption, and heuristic curriculum rationale are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee. Appendix loss expressions elaborate the existing model objectives rather than introduce a new theoretical analysis; predicate indexing and mask complementation are principally notation changes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unbiased training through masking and robustness evaluation for VidSGG/SGA. The introduction qualifies head-class preservation from no compromise to no significant compromise, although the conclusion retains the stronger wording. The revised abstract foregrounds the already established absence of additional architectural components.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 adds explanations involving relational co-occurrence knowledge and dropout-like regularization. New Section 9 explicitly discusses dataset scope, incomplete real-world corruption coverage, head-versus-tail performance tradeoffs, and limitations of recall metrics. Appendix discussions also interpret masking sensitivity and identify underperforming configurations.

D1.justification: Section 10 adds detailed filtering pseudocode, backbone-specific architecture and loss descriptions, five-epoch training caps, and reproduction difficulties for STTran/DSGDetr, including BCE-loss and ten-epoch attempts. v2 also adds a project link. These substantially expand disclosure, without proving corresponding changes to the original implementations.

R1.justification: Section 8 expands brief related-work categories into substantive discussions of cost-sensitive learning, experts, resampling, specialized architectures, and curriculum alternatives. It positions label-level masking against conventional curriculum learning and architectural debiasing, adding references on starting-small learning, boosting, active learning, and Gaussian clouded logit adjustment.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, compresses background exposition, and reorganizes the method around masked training followed by mask generation. It adds a structured appendix with an overview, extended related work, limitations, model-specific explanations, and organized experimental findings.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview diagram, predicate-level recall plots, backbone-specific diagrams, and extensive ablation tables. Some robustness rows move from the main text into expanded appendix tables. The loss equations overlapping on v1 page 6 are separated in v2, and the robustness illustration is relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: The added ablations, ordinary-recall results, fuller robustness reporting, and explicit limitations make the bias–performance tradeoff substantially easier to inspect than in v1. Equation layout also improves. However, conflicting mask conventions and fixed-versus-progressive masking descriptions leave central reproducibility questions unresolved. These problems temper the added transparency, supporting a limited net quality improvement.
